chunks: And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Baseer who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I read to you the bequest of Fatima (peace be upon her)?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, so he brought out to me a parchment: 'This is what Fatima, daughter of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), bequeathed of her wealth to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and if he dies, then to Al-Hasan, and if he dies, then to Al-Husayn; and if Al-Husayn dies, then to the eldest of my children excluding your children: Al-Dallal, and Al-Awaf, and Al-Maysab, and Burqa, and Al-Husna, and Al-Safiya, and what was for the mother of Ibrahim. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is Witness to that, and Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad, and Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam.'
ai.seo_question: What was the content of Fatima's (peace be upon her) will regarding her wealth and inheritance?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the 'Wasiyah of Fatima,' a pivotal document in Shia jurisprudence that establishes the hereditary succession of the Prophet's personal wealth (Mal al-Nabi) through the Imams. It specifically delineates the line of inheritance from Ali to Hasan, then Husayn, and finally to the eldest son of the Imams, distinguishing them from the sons of the concubines or other wives. This text serves as a key evidence for the Shia doctrine of Imamate and the continuity of prophetic authority within the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali: And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammaad Bin Usman, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> read out to you the bequest of Syeda Fatima<sup>asws</sup>?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> brought out a parchment to me, (and said): ‘This is what was assigned by Fatima<sup>asws</sup>, daughter<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, with regards to her<sup>asws</sup> wealth, to Ali<sup>asws </sup>Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>, and if he<sup>asws</sup> passes away, so to Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>; and if he<sup>asws</sup> passes away, so to Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>; and if Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> passes away, so to the eldest from my<sup>asws</sup> children besides your<sup>asws</sup> children – (The walled gardens of) Al-Dallalo, and Al-Awaaf, and Al-Maysab, and Burqa, and Al-Husna, and Al-Safiya, and what was for mother of Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Witness upon that, and A- Miqdad Bin Al-Aswad, and Al-Zubeyr Bin Al-Awaam’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said, ‘Do you like if I read the will of Fatimah, ‘Alayha al- Salam ?’ I replied, ‘Yes, I like it.’

He (the Imam) took out a document. It said, “This is what Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has willed about her assets to Ali ibn abu Talib, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. If he dies then it is for al-Hassan, if he dies then it is for al-Husayn and if al-Husayn dies then it is for the eldest of my children not your children. These walls (gardens enclosed by walls), are al-‘Awaf, al-Dalal, al- Burqah, al-Maythab, al-Husna’, al-Safiyah and Ma li ’Umm Ibrahim. Allah is witness thereof, al- Miqdad ibn Aswad and al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awam.’”
